key_insight: Instead of learning an objective that merely reproduces observed decisions, the paper learns weights that produce optimal solutions outperforming those actions in every component.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical inverse-optimization framework for decision systems where improving downstream quality matters more than matching historical choices, including MILPs.
method: Define an outperformance loss using only forward-problem oracles, making it usable for mixed-integer linear programs.
Optimize the loss with gradient-based and difference-of-convex (DC) algorithms.
Provide a generalization bound showing the failure probability at new states decreases inversely with the number of observations.
evidence_signal: Synthetic and real-data experiments show the proposed methods better predict outperforming solutions than existing inverse-optimization approaches.
watch_item: Guaranteeing a unique outperforming optimum at all training observations may be difficult in noisy or highly degenerate MILP settings.
paper_title: Outperformance Inverse Optimization: Learning Objective Functions that Outperform Agent Decisions
